Part 1

Stock Shorting Bot

Design

How the shorting bot works

Each trading day the bot shorts five of the day's top gainers into the close and holds them until the next day's rotation. It runs from cron on the Mac against the Alpaca paper account.

Time (ET)StepDetail
15:40Startcron launches daily.py --execute. The bot reads the Alpaca calendar, so half days shift automatically to 12:45 / 12:55.
15:45ScanPulls TradingView's top gainers through its scanner API. Keeps US stocks with market cap above $25M and previous close above $3, top 20.
15:45EnrichShort interest and days to cover come from FINRA and yfinance. FINRA daily short volume, SEC fails-to-deliver, Alpaca shortable/easy-to-borrow flags, and headlines from Yahoo RSS (or FMP when a key is set).
15:45ScoreYour five-item checklist. Move and volume 35%, crowding 20%, FTD 10%, catalyst 35%. Borrow is a hard gate. Squeeze traps (DTC above 10 and SI above 20%) and real de-risking news are excluded.
15:55TradeCancels leftover orders, covers yesterday's book, then shorts the top five eligible names with market orders. Sizes run 19%, 18%, 17%, 16% and 15% of equity, about 85% gross. A name held over is resized rather than closed and reopened, which avoids wash-trade rejects.
16:15SyncEquity snapshot, positions, and round trips rebuilt from Alpaca fills since 2026-10-21. Everything goes to Supabase for the dashboard.

The catalyst check earned its keep on day zero

On the first test scan (Oct 20 data), the score alone ranked MYGN #1 and BRZE #2. MYGN was up on a $210M asset sale to Labcorp, and BRZE was up 52% on a $5.66B Salesforce buyout. Shorting a buyout target is the classic way to lose. The headline classifier excluded both names before any order was placed.

Post-mortem

What went wrong the first time

The first shorting bot ran from Sep 14 to Oct 20. In five weeks the account placed three orders, all CLNN, all on Sep 15 at 15:59, and none of them shorts. It lost $2.42. The full post-mortem is here.

  • The trade gate could never open. Scoring ran before base rates were attached, so every HIGH-conviction pick was downgraded to MEDIUM. The bot only traded HIGH.
  • Failures were silent. Logs went to a git-ignored folder, and nothing outside the laptop watched them.
  • The host was unreliable. launchd never fired, a closed lid put the Mac to sleep, and cron still pointed at a renamed folder.
  • Its own backtest found no edge. Spike shorts averaged −0.81% close-to-close at a 52% win rate. 11% of trades lost more than 10%.

The new bot fixes the first three. It has no conviction tiers, every run writes a heartbeat to Supabase, and the cron points at the right folder. The fourth point, whether the strategy has an edge at all, is what the historical backtest in section 4 is testing.

Live paper results

Day one on paper: Oct 21, 2026

The 15:40 cron fired on schedule. At 15:45 the bot scanned 20 gainers; 11 were not shortable on Alpaca and one (INOD) was excluded for real news. At 15:55 it sent five short sales, all accepted, with zero problems. The 16:15 sync recorded the fills.

What day one revealed

  • Most of the gainer list can't be shorted on Alpaca. 11 of 20 names were blocked on Oct 21, and 12 of 20 on Oct 20. The bot falls through to weaker scores, which turned out to be 45 to 55 here, so the edge per pick is thinner than the checklist implies.
  • Today's moves were modest. Gains of +11% to +18% on low relative volume (0.7x to 1.8x) are well below the checklist's ideal blow-off (+20% to +100% on 5x to 10x volume).
  • Exposure is high. 85% gross short overnight with no stop. The post-mortem's backtest says single-name shorts like these have fat losing tails.
Historical backtest

Shorting strategy backtest, 2016–2026

The live configuration loses money and can wipe out the account

The current rules hold 5 shorts overnight at 19% → 15% of equity each, about 85% gross, with no stop. Backtested from 2016 to 2026, they lost money in 10 of 11 years and in both halves of the data. Two single-day squeezes would have nearly ended the account: KOSS on 2021-01-26 (−98.7% of equity) and TOP on 2023-04-27 (−96.4%). The bot is running these rules on paper now. Nothing has been changed, pending your review.

The backtest rebuilt the 15:45 "top gainers" scan for every trading day using Alpaca minute and daily bars across 6,612 stocks, including 939 that are no longer listed. The rebuilt top 20 overlaps the daily-close version by 89.8%. The bot's own scoring code ran on historical data: FINRA short interest with a publication lag, SEC FTDs, and historical Alpaca/Benzinga headlines put through the same catalyst classifier. Costs scale by price and liquidity. Borrow is charged at 15% a year, or 50% for cheap or crowded names. Rules were chosen on 2016–2021 and tested on 2022–2026, with 1,037 trials counted.

The edge is real but sits in the wrong part of the hold

Stocks that spike into the close keep rising overnight, then fade during the next session. Holding from 15:55 to 15:55 collects both legs, so they cancel, and costs turn the result negative.

What the checklist actually predicts

The proposed fix: short the next day intraday, smaller and pickier

Scan at 15:45 as today, but short the picks at the next day's open and cover at 15:55 that day. Hold up to 5 names at 10% each, 50% gross at most. Only names scoring 70+, priced at least $10, with at least $10M average daily volume.

Trades7,4145,950162174
 Per trade: mean +3.4% net, median +1.6%. Worst trade −74%, which is −7.4% of equity at 10% weight. OOS CAGR with costs doubled: 9.7%. This configuration was assembled after seeing the grid, and its deflated Sharpe at 1,037 trials is only 0.49. It makes about 30 trades a year, mostly since 2020. Paper-trade it before trusting it.

Proposed changes, none applied yet

  1. Stop holding overnight. Short at the next open (09:31 cron) and cover at 15:55.
  2. Cut size to 10% per name, 50% gross at most.
  3. Add a minimum score of 70. Allow fewer than 5 names, or none.
  4. Add a minimum price of $10 and minimum average daily volume of $10M, on top of Alpaca's borrow check.
  5. Set the FTD weight to 0. Keep the catalyst and squeeze exclusions.

Caveats: there is no historical borrow data, so a price and volume gate stands in for it. Squeeze names were likely hard to borrow then, but don't rely on that. Borrow fees are assumed, and real fees on spiking names run 50–300% a year. Some delisted names are still missing. Small-cap fills at the open will be worse than modeled.

Changes the dashboard needs from the bot

These are listed in dashboard/docs/reviews/BOT_CHANGES_NEEDED.md and left for your manual review. None have been applied to the bot.

  • Heartbeat split. The 16:15 sync overwrites the run status, so a bad run can show as healthy. The dashboard currently works around it.
  • New tables: run_events for the run log, sync_runs, and run_id on short_trades for per-run P&L.
  • monitor.py and an alerts table for intraday squeeze alerts, given that the bot has no stop.
  • Holiday rows and run timestamps, so the dashboard timeline can show actual times.

Signal study on 10 years of Alpaca bars

The signals were measured on 9 tickers from 2016 to 2026 (charts/signal_study.md):

  • Dip signals work, but the edge is small. IBS below 0.2 was positive at 5 days on 9 of 9 tickers (+0.35%). RSI(2) below 10 was positive on 9 of 9 (+0.46%).
  • Turn-of-month and the 200-day average showed nothing.
  • The best calm-vol signals: VIX/VIX3M below 0.9 means realized volatility runs 0.71x normal. Above 1.0 it runs 1.63x.
Long history

Twenty years of filter tests (2007–2026)

Alpaca's option history starts in 2024 and contains no bear market. So the regime filters were tested on Cboe's PUT, BXM, CNDR and WPUT indexes from 2007 to 2026, including 2008, 2020 and 2022. The rules were realistic: exposure could change only at the monthly roll, signals were lagged one day, and each switch cost 0.10%. Thresholds were picked on 2007–2016 and tested on 2017–2026.

Backtester

Backtester and baselines

The backtester (Options Bot/optionsbot/) runs on real Alpaca daily option bars from 2024-01 to 2026-10, about 100,000 contract histories. It infers IV and delta by inverting Black-Scholes, sizes every position as fully cash-secured, and handles expiry, assignment and early exercise before dividends. Fills cost max($0.03, 2%) per leg plus fees. 31 tests pass.

Tuning

Tuning: four strategy families

Four agents tuned in parallel under one protocol: choose parameters on March 2024 to June 2025, freeze them, then judge on July 2025 to October 2026. Every variant was counted. About 3,900 trials ran in total, so deflated Sharpe and placebo tests matter more than any single best result.

What the tuning taught, across families

  • Hold to expiry beats managing. Stops are checked at the close, so gaps overshoot them (2.56x credit on a 2x rule) and they sell at the lows.
  • Fewer round trips beats cheaper fills. The default cost model is about 3x real SPY spreads, but even with calibrated costs the managed put spread barely breaks even.
  • Lower-delta calls are the main lever for stock-backed strategies. In this up market, every short call is a drag.
  • Filters, kill switches and laddering hurt here. The sample's shocks were V-shaped, so de-risking sold near the lows.
  • In-sample rank barely predicts out-of-sample rank. The Spearman correlation is between −0.41 and 0.31 across families, so family-level patterns matter more than any single winner.

Live bot

Live options bot and code review

The paper-trading bot for the dip put spread is built in Options Bot/live/. It trades SPY, QQQ and IWM. It decides at 15:55 ET (moved from 15:50 after the re-test below) and enters with a multi-leg limit order at the mid, re-priced every 30 seconds until a 15:58 cutoff. Exits are at 50% of credit, a close above the 5-day average, after 5 days, or 1 day before expiry. Max loss is capped at 25% per position and 50% total, with a VIX kill switch. It uses only a separate Alpaca paper account's keys and refuses to run if they match the shorting bot's account. It defaults to dry run, runs a mandatory 09:45 expiry-day sweep, and has 122 tests.

Today's dry run found no signal: SPY, QQQ and IWM all closed strong. It would have sized one SPY 761/746 put spread at $1.66 credit, $1,334 max loss.

Two code reviews found 26 issues. All are now fixed and tested.

  • High:
    • A cron lock collision can silently skip a day's run, including an expiry exit.
    • A replace that races a fill can leave a spread untracked or overfilled.
    • A request timeout can leave two live orders.
    • An error mid-ladder leaves orders working.
    • The bot can't detect if the shorting bot's keys are pasted in, which would cancel the shorting bot's orders.
  • Medium:
    • A zero bid on the long leg blocks the exit near expiry.
    • Alpaca's 15:30 expiration-day handling isn't accounted for.
    • Assignment is not handled.
    • Duplicate order IDs can occur on half-dollar strikes.
  • Verified correct: leg construction, the credit/debit sign convention, cutoffs, the once-per-day guard and the paper-only refusals.

The strategy-fidelity review found that the live indicators match the research exactly: zero signal mismatches over 661 days. It also found the biggest caveat for this strategy. Deciding at 15:50 instead of the close, as the backtest did, kept only 35 of 53 research trades and cut the in-sample Sharpe from 0.76 to 0.52. A minute-bar re-test chose the new decision time:

It still leaves three minutes for order re-pricing before the 15:58 cutoff. Details: Options Bot/tuning/live_timing/ and live/README.md. Full list: Options Bot/live/REVIEW_orders.md. Literature review

What the papers say: 0DTE, longer holds, technical and news entries

Three agents read about 120 papers: academic journals, SSRN and NBER working papers, Fed, BIS and SEC notes, and Cboe research. Each topic was checked against our own backtest results. The full reviews, with per-paper notes and reference lists, are in Options Bot/research/: papers_0dte.md, papers_technical_longdated.md and papers_news.md. Citations were found via web search and have not been resolved through LibKey, because the connector needs your sign-in. Figures taken from abstracts or secondary summaries are tagged [verify] in those files.

DON'T BUILD0DTE / 1DTE bot

No paper shows an after-cost edge for a systematic same-day seller or buyer in any structure. The daily premium is about 0.01% of the index, smaller than one SPY bid-ask spread.

SUPPORTEDDip-timed put spreads, 7–60 DTE

Index returns have reverted day to day since about 2000, and short-dated put premiums rise after drops. This is the best-documented timing edge, and it backs our finalist.

FILTER ONLYNews-triggered option entries

The news drift is real but short and small-cap. LLM headline signals stop paying at about 20 bp of costs and decayed fast. Headlines are best used to avoid trades.

0DTE and ultra-short options

  • The premium is tiny per day. Annualized, the 0DTE variance premium is about 5x the 1-month one, but per day it is about 0.01% of the index (Dim, Eraker & Vilkov). The median 10:00-to-close premium is about 0.0011% of spot (Vilkov).
  • Short volatility loses after costs at every entry time. Almeida, Freire & Hizmeri use SPX 1-minute bid/ask data from 2012–2025. Delta-hedged ATM writing has a per-trade Sharpe of −0.010 to −0.042 after costs for entries from 10:00 to 14:00. Their one profitable filter stalled once daily expiries arrived in 2022.
  • A widely cited "winners" study was corrected. Vilkov's 0DTE trading-rules study had under-charged bid-ask costs by 100x. After the August 2026 correction, every strategy is negative net of costs. Iron condors and flies are the worst structure: Sharpe −0.56 at the mid and −2.67 net, annualized.
  • Retail 0DTE condors usually win but lose on average. Beckmeyer, Branger & Gayda: retail 0DTE traders lost about $241k a day from 2021–2023, and about 60% of that was costs. Retail condors had a median of +5.5% of margin but a mean of −1.1%, and the worst 5% lost the full margin.
  • Where the premium does sit:
    • At-the-money strikes. About 80% of ATM 0DTE prices exceed a risk-averse upper bound, while OTM options are often cheap.
    • Later in the day. The annualized premium rises from 1.8 at 10:00 to 3.0 at 14:00.
    • Expiries spanning CPI, FOMC or jobs reports. These are up to 7.5% dearer, and the FOMC premium is 44% larger.
    • Not 1DTE on ordinary days, which is roughly zero and negative since 2022.

Why our 1-day SPY/QQQ condor lost money (−3.8% per trade, t −3.4)

  • Wrong strikes. It sold OTM strikes, where same-day options aren't overpriced. That is why it lost even at zero slippage.
  • Wrong days. It traded every day, when the premium exists mainly on event days.
  • Wrong shape. Symmetric strikes ignore skew and upward drift, so the call side got breached in the rally, especially on QQQ.
  • Overnight risk. It was held overnight unhedged, so gaps and after-hours earnings created the max-loss days.
  • Overstated significance. SPY and QQQ trades on the same day are correlated, so the true t-stat is closer to −2.4 to −3.

Alpaca and SPY constraints

  • Alpaca rejects orders on expiring SPY/QQQ contracts after 15:30 ET, so "settle at the next close" can't be implemented as tested.
  • SPY options are American and physically settled. A short strike near the close can be assigned after hours, leaving about $55–60k of shares per contract against a $500 max-risk spread. Flatten anything near the money by 15:25.

Longer holds and technical entry signals

  • The volatility premium is a short-maturity effect. ATM straddles lose about 3% a week (Coval & Shumway). Hedging variance news from one quarter out to 14 years cost nothing on average, so shorting LEAPS earns almost no premium (Dew-Becker et al.). Front-month, near-the-money puts are the best to sell per unit of stress loss (Israelov & Tummala).
  • Weekly selling isn't better than monthly. Cboe's weekly put-write collected 39.3% gross premium a year versus 24.1% for the monthly, but it compounded lower: 5.6% vs 6.6% from 2006–2015. That matches our own 2007–2026 WPUT result.
  • Short-term mean reversion is the best-documented index signal. Daily index autocorrelation flipped from about +0.04 to about −0.04 across 20 indexes as ETFs grew (Baltussen, van Bekkum & Da).
  • Moving-average and trend rules mostly don't survive. The best Brock–Lakonishok–LeBaron rule was not significant after data-snooping correction (Sullivan, Timmermann & White). There is no significant moving-average outperformance in long samples (Zakamulin). That is consistent with our finding that the 200-day and VIX entry gates don't help.
  • Volatility-state timing has better evidence than price-trend timing. The VIX term-structure slope predicts straddle returns (Johnson 2017). The implied-minus-realized volatility spread predicts option returns (Goyal & Saretto). The premium is not reliably higher when risk rises (Cheng 2019).
  • Timing within the day and week matters. Delta-hedged index options lose about −1.0% close-to-open and gain +0.3% open-to-close (Muravyev & Ni). Option returns are much lower over weekends (Jones & Shemesh). Sellers earn overnight and over weekends.
  • Expect decay and demand a high bar. Anomaly returns fall about 58% after publication (McLean & Pontiff). New findings should clear t > 3 (Harvey, Liu & Zhu). Our 2.6-year windows give a Sharpe standard error of about 0.6, so a Sharpe of 1.0–1.5 does not clear that bar.
Our finalistWhat the literature saysVerdict
RSI(2)/IBS dip put spread, 7–14 DTETwo documented mechanisms back it: index reversal since 2000, and put premia rising after drops (Aït-Sahalia, Karaman & Mancini). The 200-day clause has the least support, so test the rule without it.SUPPORTED
SPY iron condor, 0.10Δ, 60 DTE, held to expiry60 DTE is in the well-documented harvesting band. But 0.10Δ is deep OTM, which is rated worse per unit of risk. Its 1.46 Sharpe on about 15 cycles can't be told apart from the indexes' long-run 0.5–0.7.PARTLY
QQQ wheel with 0.15Δ callsSelling OTM calls is the right direction: covered calls carry an unpaid reversal bet (Israelov & Nielsen; Bali & Murray). But most of the return is QQQ exposure, so judge it against beta-adjusted buy-and-hold.MIXED
No regime entry gatesTrend filters have weak evidence after 1990. The big short-volatility losses began from calm term structure, so gates fire after the damage. The literature prefers vol-scaled sizing over on/off gates.CONSISTENT

News- and sentiment-driven entries

  • The news drift is real but short and small-cap. Ke, Kelly & Xiu, on Dow Jones news from 1989–2020: the equal-weight long-short Sharpe is 4.21, but value-weighted it is 1.24. Large caps finish reacting in 1 day (11 bp) versus about 3 days for small caps (46 bp). The net-of-cost Sharpe peaks around 2.3.
  • The LLM headline edge dies at modest costs and decays fast. Lopez-Lira & Tang (GPT-4, 2021–2024): about 0.34% a day before costs, unprofitable at 20 bp per round trip. The Sharpe fell from 6.54 in late 2021 to 1.22 in early 2024. Most of the edge was on the short side.
  • The predicted option edge is far smaller than option spreads. The one text-to-option-return paper finds 0.33–0.49% a month (Cao et al. 2024), against a 12.6% average retail option bid-ask spread (Bryzgalova, Pavlova & Sikorskaya).
  • Scheduled and unscheduled news behave differently. Buying options pays on unscheduled news, and selling only before scheduled events (Fodor, Muravyev, Cremers & Weinbaum). Scheduled risk is priced into implied volatility in advance (Dubinsky et al.). Post-earnings drift has been nonexistent in large caps since about 2006 (Martineau). That matches our earnings tests finding no edge.
  • Retail is usually the losing side, and the speed edge is gone. Retail option buyers lose about 5–9% around earnings. Robinhood herding is followed by −3% to −4.7% returns. Macro news is priced within about 5 ms (Chordia, Green & Kottimukkalur).
  • The best use of news is as a filter. Identified news explains about half of overnight idiosyncratic volatility (Boudoukh et al.). That supports the shorting bot's catalyst check and suggests the same kind of guard on options entries.

New rules worth testing

These came from the papers. None has been backtested yet, and each would be judged on data it never saw, like everything else in this report.

RuleSourceWhy
Dip put spread with a volatility-premium filter. Enter only if VIX minus 10-day SPY realized vol > k (k = 0, 2, 4), or scale size by that spread.Goyal–Saretto; Bollerslev–Tauchen–ZhouVolatility-state timing has the best evidence. Cheap to test on our finalist.
Choose expiry by term structure. On a dip, sell 7–14 DTE when VIX9D/VIX < 1, and 30–45 DTE when it's above 1.Johnson 2017; Aït-Sahalia et al.The term-structure slope predicts which maturities are overpriced.
Enter at the close and exit at the open, comparing immediate entry with a Thursday/Friday close.Muravyev–Ni; Jones–ShemeshSellers earn overnight and over weekends. Few parameters, so little room for overfitting.
News filter on premium selling. Skip or close on fresh negative unscheduled headlines, real-catalyst or dilution news, or abnormal OTM option volume.Fodor et al.; Boudoukh et al.; Augustin et al.Uses news where it has proven value: avoiding jumps. It must improve drawdown, not just win rate.
Hype fade. A bear call spread 14–30 DTE after a hype-labelled or stale-news spike of +5% or more.Tetlock 2011; Barber et al.Stale news and retail herding reverse. Pairs naturally with the shorting bot's classifier.
0DTE test only, not a bot. Sell an SPY ATM iron fly at 10:00, 12:00 or 14:00, exit by 15:25, and include an FOMC/CPI event-day variant.Bandi–Fusari–Renò; Dim–Eraker–VilkovThe only place 0DTE premium is documented. It needs 1-minute bars, real per-leg costs and date-clustered statistics.
 Stop applies to every rule: when the literature finds no after-cost edge, our backtests did too (0DTE, earnings, news). Treat a new rule as unproven until it clears our walk-forward and a deflated Sharpe.
Part 3

Pairs Trading

Pairs trading buys one stock and shorts a similar one when their prices drift apart, betting that the gap closes. This part covers the academic literature and a 2016–2026 backtest on Alpaca data.

STILL RUNNING

One agent is reviewing the pairs-trading literature (Gatev–Goetzmann–Rouwenhorst, Do–Faff, Rad–Low–Faff, Avellaneda–Lee, Krauss and others). A second is backtesting the distance and cointegration methods on 2016–2026 Alpaca data with realistic costs and borrow fees, choosing on 2016–2021 and testing on 2022–2026. This section will update in place.

Read before acting

Caveats, bugs and next steps

Caveats

  • Short sample. The options data covers 2.6 years of mostly rising markets with three V-shaped shocks and no real bear market. Sharpe ratios carry about ±0.6 of error.
  • Daily bars only. Fills use last trades, not quotes. Greeks are inferred, and stops can't be tested intraday.
  • Hindsight in the universe. SPY, QQQ and the mega caps were chosen knowing they did well.
  • Interest not counted. Alpaca paper pays no interest on cash, which understates cash-heavy strategies by about 2–5% a year.
  • Shorting backtest limits. Historical shortability, borrow fees and market caps aren't available, so they are approximated. Delisted names are missing (survivorship bias).

Engine bugs found and worked around

These are documented in Options Bot/tuning/*/BUGS.md. The core files were not changed.

  • Spread sizing on mismatched prints booked one fictitious +$20k trade. A guard now skips spreads whose credit exceeds 60% of the width.
  • The kill-switch loss trigger can never fire on spreads.
  • The wheel's "above cost basis" rule silently falls back to strikes below basis, and its trade log omits share P&L.
  • The built-in covered call rolls ITM calls.
  • Signals fill on the same close that produced them. A one-day-lag check is reported for each finalist.
  • Forked workers crash on macOS. The fix is to set no_proxy=*.

Next steps

  1. Review the shorting bot and the branch, then merge or request changes. The shorting bot is running on paper now.
  2. Decide on the shorting bot. The backtest says the current rules lose money and carry ruin risk. You can pause the 15:40 cron, switch it to dry-run, or apply the intraday proposal in section 4 after review.
  3. Create the second Alpaca paper account and add its keys to Options Bot/.env. Then I fix the review findings, and the dip put spread runs dry for a few days before --execute.
  4. Add the SPY iron condor as the second options sleeve once the first one has run cleanly.
  5. Set up Supabase and Vercel so the dashboard goes live.
